Find the coordinates $(h,k)$ of the center of the circle above given that the points $(0,2)$ and $(8,4)$ lie on a diameter of the circle.
questions.worked_solution:
The center of the circle is located at the midpoint of the diameter. Therefore, we can calculate it using the midpoint formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}(h,k) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{0+8}{2},\frac{2+4}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{8}{2},\frac{6}{2}) \\  & =(4,3).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: The points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(0,-7)$ and $(6,1)$, respectively, and the segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ is a diameter of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.worked_solution:
The diameter can be calculated using the distance formula: 

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(0-6)}^{2}+{(-7-1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+64} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is half the diameter:

$$
r=\frac{d}{2}=\frac{10}{2}=5
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Center and Radius of a Circle on the Coordinate Plane
questions.problem:
The segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ is the diameter of a circle where the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(-7,2)$ and $(5,-6)$, respectively. Find the coordinates of the center and the radius of the circle.

The circle is centered at  $(${{field-1}}$,${{field-2}}$)$ and its radius is{{field-3}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The center of the circle is located at the midpoint of the diameter. So, we can calculate the coordinates of the center using the midpoint formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}(h,k) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{-7+5}{2},\frac{2+(-6)}{2}) \\  & =(-\frac{2}{2},-\frac{4}{2}) \\  & =(-1,-2)\end{aligned}
$$

The radius can be found by calculating the distance between the center $(-1,-2)$ and a point on the circle, such as $(5,-6):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(-1-5)}^{2}+{(-2-(-6))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-6)^{2}+{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+16} \\  & =\sqrt{52} \\  & =2\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-1,-2),$ and its radius is $2\sqrt{13}.$

questions.problem: The segment $\overset{―}{AB}$ is the diameter of a circle where the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(3b,6b)$ and $(-3b,-2b)$, respectively, with $b>0.$ Find the coordinates of the center and the radius of the circle.
questions.worked_solution:
The center of the circle is located at the midpoint of the diameter. So, we can calculate the coordinates of the center using the midpoint formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}(h,k) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{3b+(-3b)}{2},\frac{6b+(-2b)}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{0}{2},\frac{4b}{2}) \\  & =(0,2b).\end{aligned}
$$

The radius can be found by calculating the distance between the center $(0,2b)$ and a point on the circle, such as $A(3b,6b):$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(0-3b)^{2}+(2b-6b)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3b)^{2}+(-4b)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{b}^{2}+16{b}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25{b}^{2}} \\  & =5|b|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $b>0,$ we have that 

$$
r=5|b|=5b.
$$

Therefore, the center of the circle is at $(0,2b)$ and the radius is $5b.$

canonical_examples.problem: The points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $(-5,3)$ and $(-3,7)$, respectively, and the segment $\overline{AB}$ is a diameter of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The diameter can be calculated using the distance formula: 

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-5-(-3))^{2}+(3-7)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+16} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The radius is half the diameter:

$$
r = \dfrac{d}{2} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{5}}{2} = \sqrt{5}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: The segment $\overline{CD}$ is the diameter of a circle where the points $C$ and $D$ have coordinates $(7a,6a)$ and $(a,-2a)$, respectively, with $a>0.$ Find the coordinates of the center and the radius of the circle.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The center of the circle is located at the midpoint of the diameter. So, we can calculate the coordinates of the center using the midpoint formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}(h,k) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{7a+a}{2},\frac{6a+(-2a)}{2}) \\  & =(\frac{8a}{2},\frac{4a}{2}) \\  & =(4a,2a).\end{aligned}
$$

The radius can be found by calculating the distance between the center $(4a, 2a)$ and a point on the circle, such as $C(7a,6a)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{({x}_{1}-{x}_{2})}^{2}+{({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(4a-7a)^{2}+(2a-6a)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3a)^{2}+(-4a)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{a}^{2}+16{a}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25{a}^{2}} \\  & =5|a|.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $a>0,$ we have that 

$$
r = 5\vert a \vert = 5a.
$$

Therefore, the center of the circle is at $(4a, 2a)$ and the radius is $5a.$
